minor.issue: Returns 429 once the global ip_per_min limit (60/60s in config.RATE_LIMITS) is hit. Not a backend bug per se, but the frontend treats it as an invalid session (see frontend integration issue). Consider exempting /api/auth/me from the per-IP counter or raising ip_per_min, since every page load fires it.

ui_bugs.issue: LOW: the retained legacy route /api-keys is still dead on direct/hard navigation - https://<host>/api-keys returns raw {"detail":"Not Found"} from FastAPI because the ingress claims /api*. It only works via in-app <Link>. Either drop the alias or serve a client-side redirect, otherwise old bookmarks/shared links show raw JSON.

integration_issues.issue: HIGH: AuthContext.refreshUser() treats ANY /auth/me failure as 'logged out' (setUser(null)) - including HTTP 429 and network/5xx errors. Reproduced deterministically: after rapid navigation the per-IP rate limit trips, GET /api/auth/me returns 429, and the user is thrown to /login on every subsequent page load even though gb_access + gb_refresh are still valid in localStorage (verified tokens={a:True,r:True} while sitting on /login). The axios interceptor only special-cases 401, so no refresh/retry happens. Fix: only clear the user on 401/403; on 429 keep the previous user (or retry after Retry-After) and surface a 'rate limited, retrying' state.

critical_code_review_comments: Refactor verdict: clean. Workspace.jsx is now 150 lines orchestrating six 24-77 line sub-components; all data-testids survived; useMemo/useCallback boundaries are correct (statusMap update is copy-on-write, logEvents/lastError memoized on events).

AuthContext.jsx:11-21 - refreshUser's catch is too broad; it maps every transport failure onto 'unauthenticated'. This is the single functional regression risk of the memoization change and is now a reproducible user-facing logout.

lib/api.js:26-46 - the response interceptor's shared `refreshing` promise is never reset on success paths other than the happy path inside the try; also it handles only 401. Add 429/Retry-After awareness.
useLogStream.js - stable `_id: ev-${++_seq}` uses a module-level counter, so ids stay unique across remounts; onerror/onclose retry loop is sound and no longer swallows parse errors silently. Good.

rca_of_the_issue: Forced-logout RCA: every full page load of a protected route runs AuthProvider's effect -> GET /api/auth/me. RateLimitMiddleware applies a global sliding window rl:ip_per_min = 60 requests / 60s keyed on client IP to every /api path. During rapid navigation (each page load also fires estimate/keys/team/billing calls) the bucket empties and /auth/me answers 429. AuthContext.refreshUser wraps the call in a bare try/catch that does setUser(null) for any error, and lib/api.js's interceptor only attempts a token refresh on 401, so the 429 propagates unchanged. Protected then sees user==null and <Navigate to='/login'>. Tokens are never cleared, so the user is on the login screen holding a perfectly valid session - a confusing, self-healing-after-60s logout. Repro: login, then hard-navigate ~10 protected routes within 60s. Mitigation: in refreshUser, inspect err.response?.status and only null the user for 401/403; for 429 read Retry-After and retry once, keeping the existing user object.
